label: Call-processing and turnout delay (EMS lens)
note: Added once to every EMS response time (call_to_wheels_delay_min = 1.0 min). The 1.0 min figure comes from the feasibility spike (spikes/SPIKE_REPORT.md), where it was a stated parameter, not a measurement.

label: EMS response-time threshold for "within" and "isolated"
note: 8 minutes; a common planning benchmark, not tied to a specific agency standard here.

label: Which facilities count as EMS response sources
note: Baltimore City and the surrounding county fire departments stage EMS units at fire stations, but per-station unit counts are not in any source we used. Every station is one source; no unit availability.

label: Free-flow speed by OSM highway class when no maxspeed tag (mph)
value: motorway 55, motorway_link 35, trunk 45, trunk_link 30, primary 35, primary_link 25, secondary 30, secondary_link 25, tertiary 25, tertiary_link 20, unclassified 25, residential 25, living_street 10
note: Same table as the feasibility spike. maxspeed tags override; unit-less maxspeed is read as km/h (OSM convention).

label: No intersection, signal, turn, or congestion delay in the snapshot graph
note: Edge time = length / speed. Turn restrictions are not modeled. Stress futures are a later, separate layer.

label: Hex-to-node snap speed
note: snapS = straight-line distance from the hex center to the nearest drivable node / 20 km/h.

label: Snap targets are nodes with at least one non-motorway, non-link street edge
Population, zero-vehicle households and low-wage workers apportioned to hexes by area share
value: BG value x area(hex ∩ BG ∩ bbox) / area(BG)
note: Uniform density inside a land-clipped block group. Areas in UTM 18N. The part of a block group outside the study bbox is not modeled, so hex totals are smaller than block-group totals for edge block groups.

label: Jobs placed at the LODES block internal point
Zero-vehicle households
source: ACS 5-year table B25044 (owner and renter occupied, no vehicle available)

label: Low-wage workers (equity group)
value: LODES RAC CE01 (jobs with earnings <= 1250 USD/month), by home block, summed to block group
note: The architecture doc calls this field SE01; in LODES8 WAC/RAC files the earnings bins are CE01/CE02/CE03.

label: Access-lens destinations
note: Weighted k-means (weights = WAC jobs, K=8, random_state=7) over WAC blocks in the bbox; details in build_destinations.py.

label: Destination weights
note: A hex's access time is the job-weighted mean driving time to the K destinations plus snapS.

label: Access time cap (also used for unreachable destinations)
Access "added time acceptable" threshold
note: pctWithin (Access) = share of population whose added access time is at most 5 minutes.

label: Access "cut-off" block-group threshold
note: A block group is cut off when its population-weighted median added access time exceeds 10 minutes.

label: Weighted quantile definition
value: first value (sorted by value, then hex index) whose cumulative weight >= q x total weight; no interpolation

label: Shore (side of the Patapsco) classification
value: Baltimore County = 0, Anne Arundel and Howard = 1, Baltimore city by a hand-drawn harbor divider polyline
note: See pipeline/worldseed_pipeline/shore.py; cells within 250 m of the divider are 2 (ambiguous).

label: Key Bridge removal set
source: OpenStreetMap attic snapshot 2024-03-01, verified against tags and geometry by fix_keybridge.py
note: The plan expected 2 directed edges (osmnx simplified); the raw-way graph has 6 directed edges (3 per carriageway).

label: Hazmat prohibited in the Fort McHenry and Harbor tunnels
value: HAZMAT_PROHIBITED flag on the tunnel bore edges
note: Reflects the widely known hazmat restriction on Baltimore's harbor tunnels; not re-verified against MDTA rules in this build. To be confirmed.

label: Study bounding box
note: Widened from the spike so the western I-695 arc and northern Anne Arundel are in the graph.

label: Why the cross-harbor lens exists
value: the bridge's function is crossing the Patapsco
note: The region-wide job-access average barely moves when the Key Bridge is removed, because most trips never use it. The lens asks the question that matches the bridge's function: what happens to people whose jobs are on the other shore. It was defined before its results were seen; the primary threshold and every destination set are fixed by the definitions below, not tuned to results.

label: Cross-harbor cumulative-opportunity time budget (primary)
note: 30 minutes of free-flow drive time. Sensitivity at 1200 s and 2400 s is reported alongside.

label: Cross-harbor destination and origin sets
value: origins = hexes with shore 0 or 1; destinations = hexes with jobs > 0 on the opposite shore (WAC C000)
note: Ambiguous (shore 2) hexes are neither origins nor destinations: 31 hexes with about 4,200 residents and 1,500 jobs are left out.

label: Cross-harbor travel time between hexes
value: snapS(origin) + drive time node to node + snapS(destination)
note: Companion metric is the job-weighted mean of that time over all opposite-shore jobs, each time capped at 7200 s.

label: Tolerance for the simulator match on xharbor
value: 0.5 s per hex for mean time; job counts exact except hexes whose count at T +/- 0.5 s differs (accepted range lo..hi)

label: Every catalog entry is a hypothetical scenario option
note: No entry was proposed, studied or endorsed by any agency. Cost tiers are relative ($, $$, $$$) and carry no dollar figures.

label: Cross-water shuttle link speed (straight-line crossing)
note: Roughly a slow harbor craft. Straight-line distance between the two terminal nodes, no channel routing.

label: Shuttle link fixed wait (boarding, headway, unloading), added to the crossing time
note: Baked into the candidate edge time. Bounds are declared for documentation; the simulator uses the value.

label: New local road connector speed
note: Same as the default residential class speed; time = straight-line length / speed.

label: Speed factor for retimed signals on a surface corridor
note: Edge time is divided by the factor on every edge of the corridor.

label: Speed factor for incident-clearance and flow management on a freeway corridor
note: Free-flow freeway speeds are already high, so the bound is lower than for surface corridors.

label: A staging site behaves like a station (same call-processing and turnout delay, no extra delay)
